# Introduction {#sec-intro}

This paper studies endogenous timing in a two-player Tullock contest with asymmetric information. Labor and management compete over policy implementation. Labor observes its valuation of winning only after timing is chosen and before effort is set. Moving first commits; moving second preserves flexibility. The question is simple: before types are realized, who wants to lead, and how is information revealed?

The setting covers labor conflict, elections, lobbying, litigation, and rent seeking. One side often knows more about its value of victory. That changes effort, commitment, and the value of waiting. Endogenous timing is therefore also an information problem.

The benchmark is @fu2006. I keep the timing structure but allow labor's private value to follow a general distribution, using binary and uniform cases as examples. The binary case separates mean $\mu$ from dispersion $\delta$; the uniform case gives a continuous-type counterpart.

The paper has three results. First, the labor-first subgame (LM) has a unique separating equilibrium. Management's continuation best response depends only on observed effort and known prize value $V$, not on posterior beliefs. Pooling cannot be sustained, regardless of the type distribution.

Second, stage-0 timing is an ex ante payoff comparison. Labor compares $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]$ with $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]$; the type-level waiting gain only decomposes that gap after the type is realized.

Third, mean and dispersion matter jointly. Comparing only $\mu$ with $V$ is not enough; $V$, $\mu$, and $\delta$ jointly determine timing incentives.

The contribution is analytical sharpening. Relative to @fu2006, private information enters labor's prize value but not management's continuation best response. The belief channel that supports pooling in Fu is shut down. Whether the informed player leads becomes a parameter question.

The paper proceeds as follows. Section @sec-literature reviews the literature. Section @sec-setup sets up the model. Section @sec-equilibria solves SS, ML, and LM. Section @sec-timing studies timing and welfare. Section @sec-extension adds a spatial-policy extension. Section @sec-conclusion concludes.
